thread.title_full: Football: Stalled drives doom Rice Lake in defeat to Chippewa Falls - NewsBreak

author: Rice Lake Chronotype
title: Football: Stalled drives doom Rice Lake in defeat to Chippewa Falls - NewsBreak
text:
21 hours ago Drives stalling were the demise for the Rice Lake Warriors football team in a 26-6 defeat at Chippewa Falls on Friday night.
Rice Lake racked up 330 yards of offense, including 250 on the ground, but two turnovers, a turnover on downs and a missed field goal, left Rice Lake scoreless on its first four drives that all ended in Chippewa Falls territory.
Defensively the Warriors struggled to slow down the ground game of the Cardinals, who ran for nearly 250 yards and scored on all but the final possession of the game when they kneeled down for the final seconds.
Bode Schulz ran for a game-high 134 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries for the Warriors. Boedy Erickson had seven attempts for 58 yards and Ben Vande Voort totaled 46 yards on 12 carries. Through the air Vande Voort completed 6 of 10 passes for 81 yards but had an interception. Erickson was the leading receiver with three receptions for 56 yards.
Chippewa Falls' Tyler Behnke carried the ball 12 times for 103 yards and a score. Gavin Shilts added 52 on six attempts with a touchdown, and Deegan McInnis ran for a score on five carries for 43 yards. Talen Shilts also had a touchdown as he ran the ball six times for 30 yards. Quarterback Eastin Sorenson completed all four of his passes for 31 yards.
After Chippewa Falls took the opening possession 62 yards on 11 plays for a touchdown, Rice Lake looked poised to match them. The Warriors had converted on three third downs and had entered the red zone. But an intentional grounding penalty backed them up and two plays later Rice Lake faced fourth-and-7. The Warriors opted for a 29-yard field goal attempt but it came up short.
Chippewa Falls had three double-digit yard carries as the Cardinals covered 80 yards on eight plays to again find the end zone. After converting on the two-point attempt Chippewa Falls led 14-0 with five minutes before halftime during a fast-moving first half.
Rice Lake got some strong runs from Schulz to quickly cross midfield, and later Vande Voort found Erickson near the sideline for a gain of 7 yards on fourth-and-4. A pass from Vande Voort to Jack DeLawyer got the Warriors down to the Chippewa Fall 4-yard line with about 30 seconds to go before the break. Chippewa Falls stuffed a pair of runs, and on third-and-goal a fade route to Erickson in the end zone was picked off by Gavin Shilts.
The Warriors again moved deep into Cardinal territory on the first drive of the second half. Rice Lake had a manageable third-and-4 from the Chippewa Falls 22 but a false start backed the Warriors up. On fourth-and-4 Vande Voort ran a play fake but was immediately hit and taken down by Chippewa Falls' Dane Krista to force the turnover on downs.
Eight plays later the Warriors trailed 20-0 with less than two minutes to go in the third quarter. Erickson had a gain of 28 yards to cross midfield on the Warriors next drive. But two plays later the Warriors faced third-and-12. Chippewa Falls brought down Vande Voort and forced a fumble with Lucas Swope recovering.
Rice Lake had looked to have forced its first stop of the Cardinals, but Gavin Shilts ran the ball 21 yards on a fake punt on fourth down. Four plays later Behnke had a 23-yard touchdown, and with seven minutes in the game Rice Lake was down 26-0.
Vande Voort found Erickson for a gain of 46 yards to the Chippewa Falls 11-yard line to set up Rice Lake's touchdown drive. Two plays later Schulz broke across the goal line on a touchdown run of 7 yards with just 1:20 left in the game.
Chippewa Falls' win improved its record to 4-2 overall and 2-2 in the conference. Rice Lake drops to 0-6 on the season and 0-4 in the Big Rivers. It doesn't get easier for the Warriors who host New Richmond on Friday. The Tigers are unbeaten and rank fifth in the Division 2 coaches poll by Bound Wisconsin.
